Policy on greeting routines
After reading you will know how the first steps go

This page covers the first greeting at the Companion Animal Travel Desk and why it matters. New staff set the tone right away, so a calm welcome helps people relax and helps pets feel safe. Keep your voice steady, your movements easy, and your attention on the traveler and the animal together.

Start by making eye contact with the traveler and offering a simple greeting. Use plain language and avoid crowding the carrier or leash area. If a pet seems alert or uneasy, slow your pace and give space before you begin the check-in flow. Good service here is not rushed; it is steady, clear, and kind.

When a traveler arrives with a pet, listen for the basic details that guide the rest of the desk work. <<FACT F034>> After that, continue with the usual review of documents, cabin limits, and any comfort needs. If the traveler seems unsure, explain each step in a calm order so they can follow along without pressure.

For in-cabin support, remember that the staff member on the floor must stay focused on the animal’s behavior and the traveler’s comfort. <<FACT F049>> If a pet is tense, do not force contact. Let the trained staff member use patient, humane handling and keep the area quiet. That approach protects the animal and keeps the desk smooth for everyone nearby.

If a concern comes up, pass it along through the calm stepwise review used by the desk. Do not improvise, and do not promise a result before the review is complete. Your job at the first greeting is to collect, observe, and guide, not to push. A steady welcome makes the whole trip easier for the pet and the traveler.

What to remember is that a kind first greeting sets the right pace for the rest of the service.
